verdict: Gen Digital's revenue rose 12% to $1.37B as its MoneyLion-powered Trust-Based Solutions business grew 26%, and net income more than doubled to $287M.

segments.name: Cyber Safety Platform
segments.note: Security and privacy subscriptions — Norton, Avast, LifeLock and peers — sold mostly direct to consumers.

segments.name: Trust-Based Solutions
segments.note: Identity, reputation and financial-wellness products, built around MoneyLion — up 26% as the acquired business scales.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Winning and keeping subscribers for Norton, LifeLock, Avast and MoneyLion.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Product development across security, identity and financial-wellness apps.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Amortization of intangible assets from acquisitions such as Avast and MoneyLion.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $123M on the debt taken on for acquisitions, partly offset by $2M of other income.

takeaways.title: The second engine is firing
takeaways.text: Trust-Based Solutions — identity and financial wellness around MoneyLion — grew 26% to $511M, while the mature Cyber Safety Platform grew 5% to $858M. Direct revenue was $1,074M of the total.

takeaways.title: Profit more than doubled
takeaways.text: Net income rose to $287M from $134M a year ago: operating income grew 16% and the prior-year quarter carried $59M of other expense that did not repeat.

takeaways.title: Interest is the tax on the strategy
takeaways.text: Gen paid $123M of interest in the quarter — about 24 cents per dollar of operating income — the carrying cost of buying Avast and MoneyLion with debt.
